title: Refuse to stack another Battle.net Proton tree

workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Two near-simultaneous launcher invocations both pass the unlocked pgrep guard and start umu-run
leads.consequence: The guard checks for a previous process before starting its own and reserves no per-prefix lock; if both callers reach pgrep before either has entered umu-run, both call umu-run. This reproduces the stacking trigger under double-clicks or two concurrent launchers. Both return 0, neither notifies; a future click may then refuse while both headless trees remain. Add an atomic per-prefix lock held until umu-run is observable or the launch terminates, with a recheck under that lock.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus had it as an untested hypothesis (pre-existing check-then-act, narrow). Stub-only reproduction shows two concurrent invocations both pass the check; low value, not published.

leads.summary: The class-only predicate still selects unrelated applications whose class merely contains battleXnet or battlenet
leads.consequence: The regex battle.?net is not anchored and allows any one character, so an unrelated mapped window class such as unrelated-battleXnet-monitor is focused, and the installed Battle.net never launches even though pgrep would say it is absent. The stock rules use the precise steam_app_battlenet class; a separate open PR #10567 proposes battle.net.exe for the standalone install. Match supported exact classes and, where relevant, verify the chosen client belongs to this prefix.
leads.triage: reproduced only with a synthetic class 'unrelated-battleXnet-monitor'; no real application class shown to collide (Opus hypothesis 3 same area). Dropped.

leads.summary: Both focus dispatches can fail while the launcher reports success and never checks the process guard
leads.consequence: A client can disappear between clients -j and dispatch, or neither dispatcher may accept the request. The unconditional `|| true` suppresses both errors; in this branch no notification or umu-run attempt occurs and a desktop click appears to do nothing. On the next click the launcher retries the same check. At least report the failure or re-evaluate process/window state. Not reproduced against a real compositor.
leads.triage: source-only, not reproduced against a compositor; low impact. Dropped.

leads.summary: The refusal still has no visible feedback when the notification service is unavailable, and recommends a tray icon the motivating report says may not exist
leads.consequence: The helper sends via busctl --user, which exits nonzero if no org.freedesktop.Notifications responder is reachable. The launcher discards stderr, suppresses the failure and returns 0, leaving only the original stderr message, invisible from the desktop entry (Terminal=false). In the no-tray-icon case described in #13344, 'Close it from the system tray' is impossible, and 'kill its umu-run tree' gives no discoverable action. Preserve visible fallback or a safe recovery command/notification action. Source-derived, not reproduced with a real notification daemon.
leads.triage: tray/kill wording part corroborates Opus N1 (published). No-daemon part: Opus E2 shows exit 0 promptly; Omarchy ships a daemon, so not published.

leads.summary: The new headless-tree test remains green when the production pgrep search pattern is wrong
leads.consequence: The pgrep stub does not inspect argv. Mutating pgrep -af umu-run to pgrep -af definitely-not-umu leaves every test green, though the real procps matcher would miss running trees, permitting duplicate launches. Assert the command's argument and form, or use a private PID namespace with a real pgrep and test process. This is a test-validity issue, not evidence the currently shipped pattern is wrong.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2, C1/C2/D6/P1-P3); corroboration. Published as optional test improvement.

leads.summary: The new launch guard conflicts with four unstacked open Battle.net launcher PRs, especially competing guard #13619
leads.consequence: Read-only compare returns diverged for #8932, #12432, #13195, #13619. git merge-file with each PR's own merge base gives conflict markers in the launcher for all four, despite the PRs individually reporting mergeable against their own base. #13619 adds an alternate silent process-first guard, so selecting it loses this PR's notification; retaining both can double-guard. Its test's pgrep stub reports success but prints no argv: if this PR's guard wins, that other PR's 'already running' test fails because `grep -Fq` sees an empty string, while if #13619 wins this PR's `notify:` assertion fails. #8932 adds an independent window focus/wait and changes the desktop WM class, requiring intentional focus reconciliations. #12432's scale call and #13195's config arguments must end up inside the guarded launch path or cease working. No merged execution is asserted, only verified conflict hunks and source-derived consequences.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N3, merge-tree reproducer); corroboration. #13619 test-interplay detail not independently verified, not published.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `5040288`, the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13354#issuecomment-5852261991)'s behaviour findings are resolved; one wording issue is new.

- Resolved: stderr-only refusal, title-clause matches, pattern edges, style.
- Partly resolved: the `pgrep` test stub still ignores its arguments.
- Still applies: related open PRs.

### Refusal advice may not be possible

It says a copy has no window "(likely tray)" and to "Close it from the system tray or kill its umu-run tree". It also fires while `umu-run` is still starting (e.g. downloading GE-Proton). **Impact:** in #13344 (no tray icon) the only way out is a terminal command the text omits; during a slow start it advises killing that copy.

**Suggested change:** say "already running or still starting" and give one concrete way to stop a hidden copy (a command or `--exec` action).

<details><summary>Reproducer (message text at 5040288)</summary>

# Reproducer: what the refusal notification says

Reviewed head: `50402883` (omacom/omarchy PR #13354).

Whenever a `umu-run` process for `~/Games/battlenet/` exists and Hyprland lists no Battle.net window, the launcher refuses and sends the notification below. The launcher cannot tell a copy hidden to tray from one that `umu-run` is still preparing: the `umu-run` command line exists from the moment it starts, before any window. This script shows the text; it does not model why no window exists.

## Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: bash repro-notification.sh <omarchy checkout at 5040288>
# Shows what the launcher tells the user whenever a umu-run process for the
# prefix exists and Hyprland lists no Battle.net window. Nothing real is started.
set -uo pipefail

src=$(cd -- "$1" && pwd)
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'kill "${sleeper:-}" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
show() { sed "s#$tmp#\$TMP#g"; }

home="$tmp/home"
exe="$home/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Battle.net/Battle.net Launcher.exe"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$exe")" "$tmp/mock" "$tmp/fake"
: >"$exe"
printf '#!/bin/bash\n[[ $1 == clients ]] && echo "[]"\nexit 0\n' >"$tmp/mock/hyprctl"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "umu-run called: $*"\n' >"$tmp/mock/umu-run"
cat >"$tmp/mock/omarchy-notification-send" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'notification argument: %s\n' "$@"
SH
chmod +x "$tmp/mock"/*

# Stands in for a copy that is hidden to tray, or one that umu-run is still
# preparing (Proton download or runtime update) before any window exists.
printf 'import time\ntime.sleep(300)\n' >"$tmp/fake/umu-run"
(exec -a /usr/bin/python python3 "$tmp/fake/umu-run" "$exe") </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
sleeper=$!
for _ in $(seq 100); do pgrep -af umu-run | grep -Fq "$exe" && break; sleep 0.05; done

echo "running: $(pgrep -af umu-run | show)"
HOME="$home" PATH="$tmp/mock:$PATH" bash "$src/bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet" 2>&1 | show
echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

## Actual output

Bash 5.3.15, jq 1.8.2, procps-ng 4.0.7 pgrep, in an isolated sandbox with its own PID namespace:

```
running: 236 /usr/bin/python $TMP/fake/umu-run $TMP/home/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Battle.net/Battle.net Launcher.exe
Battle.net is already running (no window to focus — it may be minimised to tray).
notification argument: -u
notification argument: normal
notification argument: -g
notification argument: 🎮
notification argument: Battle.net already running
notification argument: A copy is open with no window (likely tray). Close it from the system tray or kill its umu-run tree before relaunching.
exit: 0
```

## Why the wording matters (source, not run here)

- Issue #13344: "Not one Battle.net copy had a tray icon or a window". Open PR #9245 reports that the current tray cannot open a Wine item's menu, which is where Battle.net's Exit lives.
- umu-launcher 1.4.4 (the Arch package): with `PROTONPATH=GE-Proton`, as the launcher sets, `get_umu_proton()` asks GitHub for the latest GE-Proton on each launch and `_get_latest()` downloads and extracts it when it is not installed yet, before Proton starts (`umu/umu_proton.py`). During that time the `umu-run` process exists and no window does. How long this takes on a real machine was not measured.
- umu-launcher 1.4.4 `run_command()` installs a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that forwards the signal to every descendant (`signal_handler`, `get_pstree_from_pid` in `umu/umu_run.py`), so terminating the `umu-run` process is meant to stop its tree. Not run against a real tree here.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (isolated sandbox, real `jq` and `pgrep`, stubbed `hyprctl`, `umu-run` and notification transport):

- Browser, foot and Ghostty title-only windows no longer take focus; both client classes (`steam_app_battlenet`, `battle.net.exe`) are focused, also when an unrelated window is listed first.
- A running umu-run-shaped process is detected under a `c++dev` or `John Doe` home; one for a `battlenet-old` sibling is ignored.
- The refusal calls `omarchy-notification-send` with valid arguments and exits 0; with no session bus it still exits 0 promptly.
- The new test passes on its own and under `test/shell` (run with only the two Battle.net test files), and fails against the `fc21c17` launcher and when the title clause is restored, the trailing `/` is dropped, the notification call is removed or the jq program has a syntax error.

**Optional test improvement:** the `pgrep` stub prints canned lines whatever it is called with, so a launcher calling `pgrep -f umu-run` (no `-a`, PIDs only) or a misspelt pattern still passes every case, while with the real `pgrep` that launcher starts a second copy. Adding `[[ $* == "-af umu-run" ]] || exit 2` to the stub catches both and still passes on the PR.

**Related open PRs:** the if/else re-indent now also conflicts with #12432 and #13195 (both merged cleanly with `fc21c17`); the `EOF` to `HELP` heredoc rename, unrelated to the fix, causes one of the two #13195 conflict hunks. #8932 still conflicts. #13619 is a competing fix for #13344 in the same lines, so maintainers will likely want only one. After resolving #12432's conflict, the new test calls whichever `omarchy-games-battlenet-scale` the inherited `PATH` provides (with none, it exits 127); a stub in the mock directory avoids both.
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer (pgrep stub)</summary>

# Reproducer: the test's `pgrep` stub ignores its arguments

Reviewed head: `50402883` (omacom/omarchy PR #13354).

The launcher's fixed-string check only works when `pgrep` prints full command lines (`-a`). The test's `pgrep` stub prints canned full lines whatever it is called with, so a launcher that calls `pgrep -f umu-run` (PIDs only) or searches for the wrong name still passes every assertion, while with the real `pgrep` the guard never fires. A stub that checks its arguments makes the test fail on that change and still passes on the PR as written.

## Script

Run from anywhere, with an omarchy checkout of the PR head as the argument. It works on a throwaway copy and starts only a `sleep`-like Python process whose command line looks like `umu-run`. `hyprctl`, `umu-run` and `omarchy-notification-send` are stubs; `pgrep` and `jq` are real.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Usage: bash repro-pgrep-stub.sh <omarchy checkout at 5040288>
# Works on a throwaway copy; the checkout is not modified.
set -uo pipefail

src=$(cd -- "$1" && pwd)
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'kill "${sleeper:-}" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
show() { sed "s#$tmp#\$TMP#g"; }

mkdir -p "$tmp/tree"
cp -a "$src/bin" "$src/test" "$tmp/tree/"
launcher="$tmp/tree/bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet"
test_file="$tmp/tree/test/shell.d/launch-battlenet-test.sh"

echo "== 1. Break the guard: drop -a, so pgrep prints PIDs only"
sed -i 's/procs=$(pgrep -af umu-run/procs=$(pgrep -f umu-run/' "$launcher"
grep -n 'pgrep' "$launcher" | show

echo
echo "== 2. The PR's test still passes"
bash "$test_file" 2>&1 | show
echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

echo
echo "== 3. With the real pgrep and a running umu-run-shaped process, the broken launcher starts a second copy"
home="$tmp/home"
exe="$home/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Battle.net/Battle.net Launcher.exe"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$exe")" "$tmp/mock" "$tmp/fake"
: >"$exe"
printf '#!/bin/bash\n[[ $1 == clients ]] && echo "[]"\nexit 0\n' >"$tmp/mock/hyprctl"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "umu-run called: $*"\n' >"$tmp/mock/umu-run"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "notification: $*"\n' >"$tmp/mock/omarchy-notification-send"
chmod +x "$tmp/mock"/*
printf 'import time\ntime.sleep(300)\n' >"$tmp/fake/umu-run"
(exec -a /usr/bin/python python3 "$tmp/fake/umu-run" "$exe") </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
sleeper=$!
for _ in $(seq 100); do pgrep -af umu-run | grep -Fq "$exe" && break; sleep 0.05; done
echo "running: $(pgrep -af umu-run | show)"
HOME="$home" PATH="$tmp/mock:$PATH" bash "$launcher" 2>&1 | show

echo
echo "== 4. A pgrep stub that checks its arguments makes the test catch it"
python3 - "$test_file" <<'PY'
import sys
path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path).read()
old = '# Expect -af umu-run (or similar). Emit lines only when OMARCHY_TEST_PGREP_LINES is set.\n'
new = '[[ $* == "-af umu-run" ]] || exit 2\n'
assert text.count(old) == 1
open(path, "w").write(text.replace(old, new))
PY
bash "$test_file" 2>&1 | show
echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

echo
echo "== 5. The same stricter stub passes against the unmodified launcher"
cp "$src/bin/omarchy-launch-battlenet" "$launcher"
bash "$test_file" 2>&1 | show
echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

## Suggested test change (one line in the `pgrep` stub)

```diff
 cat >"$mock_bin/pgrep" <<'SH'
```
